label: Airtable
description: Arcade tools designed for LLMs to interact with Airtable bases and records

tools.name: CreateRecords
tools.description:
Create rows in an Airtable table, up to 10 per call.

Repeating this call creates additional rows rather than replacing the first set.
`count` and `requested_count` are equal on success, and `record_ids` names the rows.
If Airtable confirms fewer rows than requested, this call raises instead of reporting
an incomplete success, because new rows do not have caller-known IDs to reconcile.

parameters.name: base_id
parameters.description: The Airtable base to write to, as a base ID starting with 'app'.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: The table to write to, as its name or a table ID starting with 'tbl'.

parameters.name: records
parameters.description: The rows to create, at most 10 per call. Each row's fields are {column, value} pairs. Pass ordinary text directly; JSON-quote text that looks like JSON. Pass numbers, booleans, null, arrays, and objects as JSON text so Airtable receives their original type.

parameters.name: typecast
parameters.description: Let Airtable convert values to each column's type and create missing select options (true), or reject values that do not already match (false). Defaults to false.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: DeleteRecords
tools.description:
Delete rows from an Airtable table, up to 10 per call.

Deleted rows are removed from the table and cannot be restored through the API.
`record_ids` holds only the rows Airtable confirmed deleted. When `count` is lower than
`requested_count`, `unconfirmed_record_ids` names the rest; re-read those before
deleting again.

parameters.name: base_id
parameters.description: The Airtable base to delete from, as a base ID starting with 'app'.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: The table to delete from, as its name or a table ID starting with 'tbl'.

parameters.name: record_ids
parameters.description: The rows to delete, at most 10 per call, each as a record ID starting with 'rec'.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: GetBaseSchema
tools.description:
Get the column names, column types and select options inside an Airtable base.

Read this before writing records: writes key on column names, a select column
rejects values outside the options reported here, and a linked-record column only
accepts record IDs from the table it names.

`views_included` is false whenever a table's views were not returned: include_views
was false, or they were left out to fit the response (then `truncated` is true). An
empty views list with `views_included` true means the table has no saved views.

Narrow with `table` when only one table matters. Airtable returns the whole base,
so leaving it empty on a wide base costs the context the records themselves need.
`truncated` says detail was left out to keep the response usable: descriptions and
views go first, then columns from the end of a table. Ask for one named table to give
it the whole response; a table still too wide returns its leading columns in order,
always at least its first, whose select options may be cut from the end.

parameters.name: base_id
parameters.description: The Airtable base to describe, as a base ID starting with 'app'.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: Describe only this table, by name or a table ID starting with 'tbl'. Leave empty to describe every table in the base.

parameters.name: include_views
parameters.description: Include each table's saved views (true), or return only its columns (false). Defaults to false.

output.description: The tables in the base, with their columns

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: GetRecord
tools.description:
Get a single Airtable row by its record ID.

Returns every column unless fields narrows it. Long cell values are clipped the same
way they are in a listing, and `truncated` says when that happened. A record ID that
does not exist, or was deleted, comes back as a refusal that does not distinguish
the two.

parameters.name: base_id
parameters.description: The Airtable base to read from, as a base ID starting with 'app'.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: The table to read from, as its name or a table ID starting with 'tbl'.

parameters.name: record_id
parameters.description: The record to retrieve, as a record ID starting with 'rec'.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Only return these columns, by column name. Defaults to every column.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: ListBases
tools.description:
List the Airtable bases this authorization can reach, with permission levels.

Returns bases in Airtable's default order.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Continuation token from a previous call's next_cursor. Leave empty to start from the first page.

output.description: A page of accessible Airtable bases

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: ListRecords
tools.description:
List rows from an Airtable table, optionally filtered, sorted and column-limited.

Use this when the condition combines columns, or compares numbers or dates. To match
one column against plain text, use the record search tool instead.

Returns records in the view's order, or Airtable's default order when no view is
given, unless sort_field overrides it.

parameters.name: base_id
parameters.description: The Airtable base to read from, as a base ID starting with 'app'.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: The table to read from, as its name or a table ID starting with 'tbl'.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Only return records visible in this view, by view name or view ID. Leave empty to read the whole table.

parameters.name: filter_formula
parameters.description: An Airtable formula that must evaluate true for a record to be returned, in the form {Column Name} = "value". Any literal value inside the formula must have its double quotes and backslashes escaped by the caller; this parameter is sent as written. To match one column against plain text, use the record search tool instead, which escapes the term for you. Leave empty for no filter.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Only return these columns, by column name. Defaults to every column.

parameters.name: sort_field
parameters.description: Column name to sort by. Leave empty to use the table or view's own order.

parameters.name: sort_direction
parameters.description: Direction to sort by when sort_field is set. Defaults to ASCENDING.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum records to return (1-100). Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Continuation token from a previous call's next_cursor. Leave empty to start from the first page.

output.description: A page of records from the table

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: SearchRecords
tools.description:
Find rows in an Airtable table whose column matches a search term.

Use this to match one column against text: quotes and backslashes in the search term
are escaped, so arbitrary text is safe to pass. Use the formula-based listing instead
when the condition combines columns or compares numbers or dates.

Returns records in the table's order unless sort_field is given.

parameters.name: base_id
parameters.description: The Airtable base to search, as a base ID starting with 'app'.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: The table to search, as its name or a table ID starting with 'tbl'.

parameters.name: field_name
parameters.description: The column to match against, by column name.

parameters.name: search_text
parameters.description: The text to look for in that column.

parameters.name: exact_match
parameters.description: Require the whole cell to equal search_text (true), or match any cell containing it, ignoring case (false). Defaults to false.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Only search records visible in this view, by view name or view ID. Leave empty to search the whole table.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Only return these columns, by column name. Defaults to every column.

parameters.name: sort_field
parameters.description: Column name to sort matches by. Leave empty to use the table's own order.

parameters.name: sort_direction
parameters.description: Direction to sort by when sort_field is set. Defaults to ASCENDING.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum records to return (1-100). Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Continuation token from a previous call's next_cursor. Leave empty to start from the first page.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: UpdateRecords
tools.description:
Change columns on existing Airtable rows, up to 10 per call.

Only the columns supplied are written; every other column is left untouched.
`count` is how many rows Airtable confirmed. When it is lower than `requested_count`,
`unconfirmed_record_ids` names the rest; re-read those before updating them again.

parameters.name: base_id
parameters.description: The Airtable base to write to, as a base ID starting with 'app'.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: The table to write to, as its name or a table ID starting with 'tbl'.

parameters.name: records
parameters.description: The rows to change, at most 10 per call. Each entry names the record to update and the columns to set on it as {column, value} pairs; columns left out keep their values. Pass ordinary text directly; JSON-quote text that looks like JSON. Pass numbers, booleans, null, arrays, and objects as JSON text so Airtable receives their original type.

parameters.name: typecast
parameters.description: Let Airtable convert values to each column's type and create missing select options (true), or reject values that do not already match (false). Defaults to false.

summary:
Arcade's Airtable toolkit lets LLMs read and write Airtable bases and records through the Airtable REST API.

## Capabilities

- **Discovery** — List accessible bases with permission levels; retrieve a base's full schema (tables, column names, types, select options, linked-record targets, and saved views) before writing to avoid type or value mismatches.
- **Record retrieval** — Fetch a single record by ID or list records with optional filtering, sorting, column limiting, and view scoping; use the dedicated search tool for single-column text matching and the formula-based list tool for multi-column or numeric/date conditions.
- **Record writes** — Create up to 10 rows per call (repeating appends, never replaces); update specific columns on existing rows without touching others (up to 10 per call); delete rows permanently with partial-confirmation handling via `unconfirmed_record_ids`.
- **Auth introspection** — Confirm which Airtable account the current authorization belongs to and which scopes have been granted.

## OAuth

This toolkit uses OAuth 2.0 via the **Airtable** provider. See the [Arcade Airtable auth provider docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/airtable) for setup details.
